title: Hold a polymer beam at 1 mm and then 2 mm of bend on a lever test stand, unloading in between
instruction: Put the beam on the test rollers. Using the stand's lever, hold its centre at 1 mm deflection for a second, let the lever up to zero load, hold 2 mm for a second, then let the lever up and return the beam to a cradle.
context: Materials labs run quick three-point bend checks to compare the stiffness of polymer lots. A robot doing this must centre the bar on the rollers, work the stand's lever to hold set deflections while the gauge reads the load, unload without disturbing the bar, and put it away. Category Other: materials-research automation.
setup: Full-size Mark-10 ES05 lever test stand (162.1 x 99.1 mm base, 355.6 mm high, 38 mm travel) with AC1060 base plate, G1095 lower bend fixture (10 mm rollers at 150 mm span), G1097 upper anvil and M5-20 100 N force gauge. The stand's spring-loaded lever (about 105 mm, black 26 mm knob, scaled from the maker drawing) rests 40 degrees above horizontal on the right of the head; the head is set so the nose rests 6 mm above the bar. A low-force 0.01 mm digital indicator (0.2 to 0.5 N, for example Mitutoyo 543-715) hangs from the lower fixture and reads the bar's centre deflection from below; the robot reads the gauge and indicator screens. In the simulation a 190 x 90 mm display lying flat to the right of the stand repeats force (N) and deflection (mm). Specimen: TIVAR 1000 UHMW-PE bar, 200 x 25 x 10 mm, 46.5 g, white, with three small black witness marks on its front face at mid-span and over each roller. Two machined aluminium cradles, 70 x 220 x 10 mm bases with two 40 x 25 x 20 mm saddles each, side by side on the left of the bench, bar centres at X=200 (far) and X=110 (near), Y=130 mm. The load axis is X=320, Y=0 mm (X away from the arms, Y left, Z up from the bench). Layout A starts the bar on the far cradle, layout B on the near one; the stand and cradles are fixed. Trials A and B are averaged; the screenshot is A.
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial (latched) if the bar leaves the table, the stand moves over 5 mm, the gauge reads over 50 N, the bend exceeds 4 mm, an arm comes within 5 mm of the bar or touches it with over 0.5 N while the nose load is over 2 N, an arm presses the bar onto the rollers with over 0.5 N, or, from the first nose load over 2 N until the second reading, the bar slips over 1 mm on a roller, loses a roller or is lifted. Otherwise 0.25: released on both rollers, centre within 2 mm of the load axis, yaw and tilt within 2 degrees, arms over 10 mm away, still 1 s (lost if moved). 0.5: a reading at 1.0 +/- 0.2 mm deflection with nose load over 2 N, still (under 0.03 mm change per 50 ms) for 1 s. 0.75: then an unload to 0.2 mm or less and under 2 N, then a reading at 2.0 +/- 0.2 mm held 1 s. 1.0: both readings, nose under 2 N, residual deflection 0.2 mm or less, bar on a cradle within 5 mm and 1 mm height, arms at least 30 mm away, bar still 2 s. Gauge and indicator displays, video and a ruler establish each condition.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz) per layout
reset_notes: 1. Check the 150 mm span and witness marks. 2. Put the bar on the far cradle for A or the near one for B. 3. Let the lever return to its rest stop and zero the indicator with the bar unloaded on the rollers. 4. Clear both arms; run A then B.
fidelity: Declared bending model: one centre spring of 17,778 N/m from E = 600 MPa and k = 48EI/L^3 (about 17.8 N at 1 mm); no FEM, creep or material calibration. Damping 4 N s/m and friction 0.2 are estimates. Force is the native nose contact; deflection is the ideal centre-to-support chord, without the real indicator's 0.2 to 0.3 N plunger force. Lever length, rest angle and 18 mm/rad drive are scaled from the maker drawing; the 0.3 N m/rad return spring is estimated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (layout A 0.0, layout B 0.0); demo: 1.0 (layout A 1.0, layout B 1.0)
